meta.name: Retromon Big Packs (Willibab)
meta.description: Creature art for Monster Tactics. Source: 'Retromon Big Pack 1-4' by Willibab (https://willibab.itch.io/). Free for personal/commercial use with credit - see LICENSE.txt. The original sheets ship with an opaque near-white background baked into every frame (not real alpha transparency); each frame here was re-exported with a border flood-fill so the background is transparent while enclosed white details (eyes, teeth, highlights) are preserved.

frameIndexing: Frame index = row * 9 + col (Phaser's default row-major order for a loaded spritesheet), 0-indexed from the top-left.

wiredSpecies.note: Current SPECIES/ENEMY_SPECIES entries in data/monsters.js all use sheetKey 'retromon-b1'. Enemy species are the evolved form of the same visual line as the matching player species, so wave 'monsters' are the grown-up version of what you can catch.

unusedFrames: big-pack-1.png has 72 frames total and only 8 are wired up (see wiredSpecies above) - there's a lot of room to add more species from the same sheet before touching big-pack-2/3/4.

contents: Retromon Pack 1/2/3/4/5.7z and Retromon_Super_Pack_01/02.7z - these are NOT simple per-cell monster grids like the Big Packs. They're Willibab's palette-recolor reference sheets: multiple color-variant panels of the same creatures plus swatch columns, laid out irregularly. A naive fixed-grid slice (which is what was tried initially) produces garbage - each would need manual per-panel cropping to be useful.

Willibab_Trainer_Sprites.png / Willibab_Alternative_Back_Sprites.png - player/trainer character walk sprites. Same opaque-background issue as the Big Packs (blue matte this time, not white) - not yet defringed or wired into any scene.
